newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Engen shrs near year low on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Engen shrs near year low on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in South African oils and fuel group Engen Ltd slid to their lowest level in just short of a year on Tuesday after a warning that second half earnings may drop below those recorded in the first six months.
Releasing results for the half year to February 28 on Monday, Engen head Rob Angel said the bottomline would come under pressure from lower oil prices.
On Tuesday morning Engen stocks slid over 1.5 percent to 22.75 rand, their worst level since April 10 1996 when they touched 22.37 rand.

"The negative is obviously the comment made that they don't think earnings will be any better in the second half...The market doesn't like companies with no growth in earnings," said Paul Carter, an analyst at ING Barings.

Angel said on Monday that if current rand crude and product prices continued to the 1997 financial year end, Engen would in the second part of the year report an inventory loss of around 38 million -- similar in size to a gain in the first half.

"In these circumstances, and ignoring the beneficial impact of any increase in regulated marketing margins, the company's net income for the second half of the financial year would be lower than that reported for the first half," Angel said.
In the first six months Engen reported earnings at 107.0 cents a share, up 21.6 percent on a year ago and slightly better than analysts' forecasts of around 103 cents.
Engen's share price has been declining steadily from 29 rand at the end of January, weighed by concerns about year results and in line a donwngrading of the whole sector, analysts said.
"There was possibility a recognition in the share price that earnings for the full year were not going to be as good as originally anticipated," another analyst said.
"The sector as a whole has also be derated somewhat. Sasol Ltd and AECI have also come off. There is less appetite for the sector."
By 1030 GMT Engen shares had clawed off their lows, settling unchanged at 23.10 rand after briefly edging up to a high of 23.40 in volume of 169,000 shares.
